question.problem: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=(x-1)(x-9)$ is $x=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
From the equation $y=(x-1)(x-9),$ we can tell that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=9.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{1+9}{2} \\  & =\frac{10}{2} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x=5.$
